scientific_question: Among species that actually share geographic space, does lineage similarity improve out-of-species prediction of post-IBD mitochondrial genetic differentiation?

source.interpretation: species-disjoint prospective replication panel within the same source database; not an independent database replication

response_blind_panel.marker_family: COI/COX1 under the already frozen alias rule
response_blind_panel.selection_rule: after geometry-only one-panel selection and exclusion of all parent Phase-1 species, scan the rank in order and retain the first 250 species passing the frozen endpoint-disjoint geometry requirement; no genetic outcome may enter replacement
response_blind_panel.split: lower 125 hash ranks training; upper 125 evaluation

co_distribution.directed_metric: for source s and target t, fraction of target edge midpoints within 500 km of at least one source edge midpoint
co_distribution.rationale: requires material shared geographic support at the same spatial scale as the frozen TTF field; threshold selected using response-blind geometry only

primary.name: order_given_geography
primary.target_set: evaluation species with >=3 geographically co-distributed training species from the same non-empty taxonomic order
primary.baseline_field: all geographically co-distributed training species, each with the inherited species-equal TTF weighting
primary.conditioned_field: same-order subset of the geographically co-distributed training species, each with the inherited species-equal TTF weighting
primary.estimand: Delta_order_given_geo = species-equal mean over fixed supported targets of [C_same_order_geo - C_all_geo]
primary.interpretation_if_qualified_positive: lineage similarity increases spatial transferability among species that share geographic support; taxonomic order is a lineage-similarity proxy, not a measurement of dispersal ability or shared demographic history

secondary_geometry_diagnostic.name: geography_restriction
secondary_geometry_diagnostic.target_set: evaluation species with >=3 geographically co-distributed training species
secondary_geometry_diagnostic.estimand: Delta_geo = species-equal mean over fixed supported targets of [C_geo - C_all]
secondary_geometry_diagnostic.inferential_status: development diagnostic until a separate geography-conditioned positive-control family is prospectively frozen and qualified

future_dispersal_extension.rule: do not substitute taxonomic order for movement ability; a dispersal or life-history similarity test requires an independently sourced trait table, a predeclared missing-data rule, and adequate coverage frozen before conditional nucleotide identity is opened

support_decisions.same_class: not a confirmatory condition because the panel is overwhelmingly Insecta and class is too coarse
support_decisions.same_family: not a confirmatory condition because response-blind support is insufficient

phase3_qualification.primary_inference_candidate: one-sided centered held-out-species bootstrap of per-target paired Delta_order_given_geo
phase3_qualification.private_null: one independent spatial boundary field per species
phase3_qualification.positive_control: one shared spatial boundary field per frozen taxonomic order; different orders receive independent fields
phase3_qualification.failure: NOT_EVALUABLE; do not open conditional-panel nucleotide identity

empirical_opening.rule: only after exact new-panel character-mask admissibility and exact-geometry conditional synthetic qualification PASS

forbidden: using any parent-panel genetic score to choose the new species, geographic threshold, taxonomic level, source set, or split
testing family-level transfer after seeing its sparse support
calling taxonomic order a direct measurement of dispersal ability
opening nucleotide identity before the new panel passes its exact-geometry conditional qualification
searching post hoc across radius, coverage threshold, taxonomic rank, marker, subset, bandwidth, or alpha for a favorable conditional result
rewriting the completed parent one-shot result
